run.question: I'm investigating an error in trace TRACE-ERR-X9K2M. Check Elasticsearch and tell me which service failed and what the error was.

report.summary: Elasticsearch answers the question. In index app-245-apm-traces, trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M matched exactly 2 documents (17:06:00Z and 17:06:00.050Z). The failing component recorded in the trace is service payment-gateway: its span span-pay-err on operation authenticate_payment carries error.type ConnectionTimeout, error.message 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729' and http.status_code 503 with duration_ms 5180; its parent span span-gw-err belongs to service api-gateway (operation POST /api/payment) and also returns 503 (duration_ms 5234). The error stack trace shows payment_gateway's auth_client calling http_client.post(auth_url, ..., timeout=5.0), consistent with the ~5.2 s span. This is the only error document in the index: aggregation by_service gives api-gateway 11, payment-service 10, payment-gateway 1; by_status gives 200=20 and 503=2; by_error_type gives ConnectionTimeout=1. The 10 preceding traces (16:52–17:01) on the api-gateway POST /api/payment path succeeded (200). Whether the authentication service named in the message actually failed is not observable here: it has no document in the only Elasticsearch index. Jaeger and Prometheus were unavailable in this Run, so no span graph, error-rate or latency baseline could be obtained, and the trace_id is not a hex id, so the Jaeger lookup could not be attempted.

claims.text: Index app-245-apm-traces is the only index returned by the index listing (1 index, 22 documents) and its mappings include trace_id, span_id, parent_span_id, service, operation, http.status_code, duration_ms and error.type/message/stack_trace.

A query for the string TRACE-ERR-X9K2M in app-245-apm-traces returned total 2 documents (relation eq), both at 2026-11-23T17:06:00Z / 17:06:00.050Z, i.e. the trace consists of exactly these two indexed spans in this index.

Span span-pay-err (service payment-gateway, operation authenticate_payment, parent_span_id span-gw-err, trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M, @timestamp 2026-11-23T17:06:00.050Z) records error.type ConnectionTimeout, error.message 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729', http.status_code 503 and duration_ms 5180.

Span span-gw-err (service api-gateway, operation POST /api/payment, trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M, @timestamp 2026-11-23T17:06:00Z) records http.status_code 503 and duration_ms 5234, and it is the parent reference of the failing payment-gateway span.

The failing span's stack trace (truncated at 2000 characters in the view) shows payment_gateway/handlers/payment_handler.py process_payment calling auth_client.authenticate, which calls http_client.post(auth_url, json=payload, timeout=5.0) in payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py.

The failing span's http.response.body (truncated at 2000 characters) is an HTML 'Payment Gateway Error' page titled 'Service Unavailable' stating 'The payment authentication service is currently unavailable.'

Aggregations over all 22 documents in the window (16:08:03–17:08:03Z) give by_service api-gateway=11, payment-service=10, payment-gateway=1; by_status 200=20, 503=2; by_error_type ConnectionTimeout=1, i.e. the single error document in the index is the payment-gateway span above.

The other 10 traces in the index (2026-11-23T16:52:00Z through 17:01:00Z) each consist of api-gateway POST /api/payment (200, duration_ms 245) with child span service payment-service, operation process_payment (200, duration_ms 180, no error fields); in the error trace the child span is instead service payment-gateway on operation authenticate_payment.

The api-gateway -> payment-service path is not shown failing in this index: all 10 payment-service spans at 16:52–17:01Z returned http.status_code 200 with no error.type/error.message, and api-gateway returned 200 in 10 of its 11 spans; its only 503 is the span of TRACE-ERR-X9K2M itself.

The deepest cause is likely the authentication endpoint that payment-gateway's auth_client calls at auth_url (a 5.0 s client timeout was exceeded; span duration 5180 ms): that dependency appears unresponsive or too slow. This is not verified — no span, document or log for any authentication service was found in app-245-apm-traces (all 22 documents were listed, one of which is the payment-gateway error span that mentions 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729').

payment-gateway and payment-service may be distinct components (or the payment path may have been routed to a different component) because successful traces show child service payment-service/process_payment while the error trace shows child service payment-gateway/authenticate_payment under the same api-gateway operation POST /api/payment. The two-document sample cannot establish routing or call-graph structure.

Rejected as the failing service: payment-service. Its own spans on this path (service payment-service, operation process_payment, 16:52–17:01Z) are all 200 with no error fields; the error document belongs to service payment-gateway, not payment-service.

A pod listing across all namespaces (32 pods) shows only service payment (pod payment-6f7bc865d6-wwqnm, Running, ready, 0 restarts) in the otel-demo namespace; no pod or controller named payment-gateway, api-gateway, payment-service or any authentication service exists in the queried cluster, and all listed pods are Running/ready with 0 restarts and empty lastState.

Read the referenced application's own logs/metrics for the authentication endpoint called at auth_url and for payment-gateway (error code AUTH-4729, ConnectionTimeout with a 5.0 s client timeout) in a source that actually holds them; the only Elasticsearch index available (app-245-apm-traces) holds trace documents only and Jaeger/Prometheus were unreachable in this Run.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, and traces_query_trace_by_id returned INVALID_PARAMS for the supplied trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M (not a hex id), so no span graph beyond the 2 Elasticsearch documents and no span status tags could be checked.

Prometheus label discovery returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (get_label_values on traces_span_metrics_calls_total for service_name and status_code), so no error-rate, latency baseline or time series for payment-gateway, payment-service or any authentication service could be read.

The authentication service referenced in 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729' has no document in app-245-apm-traces; a full listing of all 22 documents and the trace-scoped query show no span or log for it, so its own health is unknown rather than proven bad.
elasticsearch_list_indices returned only app-245-apm-traces (trace documents), so no application log index, nginx/ingress logs or auth-service logs were available.
The Elasticsearch searches used the default time filter 2026-11-23T16:08:03Z–17:08:03Z; documents outside that window, and any documents not ingested, are unknown.

The Kubernetes cluster queried contains no objects named payment-gateway, api-gateway, payment-service or an authentication service, so the cluster state cannot confirm or refute the health of the services in this trace; the pod listing is also post-incident state.
The all-namespace Kubernetes events query returned no data (total_items_processed 0), so events neither confirm nor explain the failure.

The error.stack_trace and http.request.body / http.response.body fields were truncated at 2000 characters by the tool, so the full stack trace and request payload are unknown; http.request.body contained card-number/cvv style fields that were not readable in full.
Which component owns the auth_url endpoint, and whether the 5.0 s timeout or a network path is the cause, cannot be determined from the available evidence.

Inspect the authentication service named by error code AUTH-4729 (reachable at payment_gateway auth_url) for its own errors, latency and availability at 17:06:00Z.
Compare the observed 5180 ms payment-gateway span against the 5.0 s http_client timeout in auth_client.py to determine whether a raised timeout or a faster auth dependency is appropriate.
Retrieve payment-gateway application logs for span-pay-err / the request at 2026-11-23T17:06:00.050Z to get the full stack trace and the auth_url actually used.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.
